notes: Oxford Cryosystems does not publish the PheniX chamber dimensions; the only dimensions in the spec table are for the K450 helium compressor (64 x 61 x 54 cm, 100 kg), so the outer block carries those with the location flagged, and the chamber itself is listed under not_found. Verified facts for the scene: two-stage GM coldhead built into the Phenix body, fed by the K450 compressor through high-pressure hoses via a rotating seal so the stage can do theta-2theta scans; sample is conduction-cooled on a 20 mm Cr-plated Cu plate in vacuum (1e-4 mbar per PANalytical leaflet); mylar radiation shield window 0.005 mm and Kapton lid window 0.25 mm giving a 120 degree X-ray view; 12-290 K, +/-0.1 K, 20 K in 40 min, 12 K in 60 min, warm-up 45 min; optional vacuum system continuously pumps the vacuum space and rotating seal; cooling water 5 L/min at 18 C (3 kW chiller, not supplied). Wood et al. 2018 (PMC5988005) confirms the standard PheniX is two-stage and 12 K base but dimensions its PheniX-FL variant only.
